A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AOT research work. The main text, eight tables, six figures, equations, and supplementary Sections 6–11 are readable and can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-understanding benchmark results, computational measurements, ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised AOT scores in the main and supplementary tables.

M1.justification: Local/global anchor selection, intra-frame and inter-frame optimal transport, temporal-token retention, and Sinkhorn inference remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2. Expanded future-work suggestions do not introduce an implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVBench, EgoSchema, LongVideoBench, and VideoMME, including the same frame-count variations and qualitative examples. The expanded discussion of 3D/4D applications does not report evaluations in those domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: FastV, PDrop, DyCoke, VisionZip, PruneVid, and FastVID remain the main baselines. Newly cited methods such as SparseVILA are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 7 retain the model sizes, frame counts, token budgets, anchor counts, metrics, and optimization settings. The changed FLOP entries are reported cost revisions; neither version documents a corresponding change in evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Updated full-AOT scores slightly revise the existing ablation evidence. In Table 5, full AOT moves from above the variant without intra-frame OT on MVBench (57.2 versus 57.1) to below it (57.0 versus 57.1). The ablation configurations, sensitivity tests, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for the experiments. The point-estimate reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Several AOT scores are revised under the same stated settings: Table 1's 25%-retention average changes from 58.1 to 58.5, and Table 2's 15%-retention average changes from 57.3 to 57.5. Corresponding appendix and ablation entries are updated. Tables 1 and 6 also exchange AOT's 10%/15% FLOP entries between 3.4T/8.3% and 5.2T/12.7%, without an accompanying protocol explanation.

T1.justification: The optimal-transport formulation, aggregation equations, and supplementary Sinkhorn derivation remain mathematically unchanged. Added explanatory wording and equation-spacing edits introduce no new assumptions, definitions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims about training-free local/global token aggregation. The introduction also retains the headline claim of 90% token pruning, 8.3% FLOPs, and 97.6% performance preservation.

C2.justification: Section 11 expands the existing auxiliary-supervision suggestion into specific prospective uses of depth, camera motion, correspondence, and trajectories for spatial reasoning. Existing limitations remain unchanged. Section 7 also softens the description of 100 iterations from optimal to a default setting.

D1.justification: New acknowledgments disclose access to LEONARDO and MareNostrum5 computing resources, without specifying a changed experimental allocation. The A100 hardware specification, hyperparameters, implementation instructions, and project-webpage link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography grows from 79 to 84 works, adding SparseVILA, Token Reduction Should Go Beyond Efficiency in Generative Models, PerLA, T2TD, and UVMap-ID. These additions modestly extend related-work and future-work context without redefining the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and notation clarifications, adds corresponding-author information and acknowledgments, and expands the future-work paragraph. The main section order and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 move from PDF page 7 to page 6, and the supplementary opening and some figure/table spacing are reformatted. All figures and tables are retained; the figures show the same content.

improvement.justification: Limited clarifications and expanded future-work discussion are outweighed by newly inconsistent efficiency reporting. In v1, Table 1 supports the introduction's combination of 10% token retention, 8.3% FLOPs, and 97.6% retained performance. In v2, Tables 1 and 6 assign 12.7% FLOPs to that retention level, while the introduction retains the old claim without explanation. This weakens the internal consistency of a central efficiency claim.
